title: Matrices: shape, traversal, and linear storage
goal: Translate a coordinate to an index and check a rectangular shape at its boundaries.

prerequisites.text: Modules 1–2: expressions, comparisons, types, references, and checked cin.
Follow the prerequisite links: cpp.one-dimensional-arrays. New constructs are introduced before the assignment.

sections.title: Two coordinates
paragraphs: A seating table has two dimensions. In a 2×3 shape, the second row starts after three seats, so coordinate (1,2) points at the sixth and final value.

A matrix has rows rows and cols columns. Element (r,c) is valid when 0<=r<rows and 0<=c<cols. In std::array<std::array<int,3>,2>, the outer size is two rows and the inner size is three columns. A built-in int a[2][3] is also an array of rows.

a[r][c] first selects a row and then its element. Swapping indices does not safely transpose an arbitrary matrix: rectangular dimensions may produce out-of-bounds access. Check both coordinates independently.

sections.title: Nested traversal
paragraphs: The outer loop visits rows; the inner loop visits columns in the current row. Set rowSum=0 before the inner loop and initialize total once before both loops. Mixing these state levels leaves only the final row’s sum.

With rows*cols elements, a complete traversal is O(rows*cols). If either dimension is zero, there are no elements. The lab explicitly permits zero dimensions so the algorithm never depends on a[0] existing.
The outer counter selects a row and the inner counter selects a column. For 2×0 there are two outer steps but no element in either row.

sections.title: A flat buffer
paragraphs: In row-major storage, the index is r*cols+c. The preceding r rows occupy r*cols positions, then c selects a column. In a 2x3 matrix, (1,2) maps to 5, the last of six elements. This follows from the representation rather than a magic conversion.

vector<int> data(rows*cols) creates elements, unlike reserve. Validate dimensions before multiplying. Dimensions up to 10 give at most 100 elements; values in -1000…1000 have an absolute total at most 100000.
In r * cols + c the stride is the source column count. A square test may hide an accidental substitution of rows for cols.

tables.caption: One buffer with shape 2×3
rows: Index 1 × 3 + 0 = 3, value 4. This begins the second row.

sections.title: A coordinate into an index
paragraphs: Substitute r = 1, c = 2 and cols = 3. Name the index separately from the value read.

sections.title: Rectangularity and nested vectors
paragraphs: vector<vector<int>> can contain rows of different lengths. Its type does not establish rectangularity. Before running a matrix algorithm, verify that every row has cols elements; define cols separately when the outer vector is empty.

Flat storage simplifies the total size but requires an indexing formula. Nested storage exposes rows clearly but gives each row a separate owned buffer. Choose a representation for the required operations rather than bracket appearance.
Rows {1, 2} and {3} can belong to the same nested vector. For a matrix, verify equal lengths first or maintain rectangularity by construction.

sections.title: Rows, columns, and transposition
paragraphs: A column sum fixes c and varies r. A square matrix’s main diagonal has r==c; a rectangular generalization has length min(rows,cols) if the contract defines it that way. Never assume square shape without validation.
A transpose has cols rows and rows columns. Write result[c*rows+r]=data[r*cols+c] into a new buffer. An in-place transpose requires another algorithm and is not an implicit requirement here.
Transposition maps (r,c) to (c,r). A 2×3 shape becomes 3×2, so the new row stride is 2.

sections.title: Transposing 2x3
paragraphs: Before running, draw three rows of two cells. Move 2 and 4 to their new coordinates.

reveal.title: Reveal output and trace execution
paragraphs: The original first column becomes the new first row. A rectangular example makes the dimension swap visible.

sections.title: Shape tests
paragraphs: A square example can hide reversed dimensions. Include 2x3 and 3x2, one row, one column, and a zero dimension. Label original positions with distinct values to expose permutations.

Keep a table of (r,c,index,value), expected sums, and operation counts. Incomplete or excess input must reject the whole record as invalid. Next, character sequences introduce another distinction: a byte, a character, and a terminator are different things.
Distinguish 0×3 from 2×0. Neither contains elements, but a row report for 2×0 has two sums and one for 0×3 has none.

tables.caption: Same element count, different rows
rows: No rows. Total 0 and a blank second output line.
Two rows with no elements. Total 0 and a second output line of 0 0.

sections.title: Now try your own task
paragraphs: An operator wants a grand total and a sum for each row. The order of rows is retained even with zero columns.
For 2×3 mark the boundaries between input rows. For 2×0 draw two empty rows.

feedback: Correct: three rows of two values.

selfcheck.prompt: What is the flat index of (1,2) in a 2x3 matrix?
What shape is the transpose of 2x3?

selfcheck.feedback: Each row has an independent size.

selfcheck.prompt: How many elements does shape 2x0 contain?
selfcheck.feedback: Two empty rows contain no elements.

selfcheck.prompt: What is needed to accept this lab?
options: Source, actual results, original tests, and a contract explanation
selfcheck.feedback: A progress flag is not evidence of independent mastery.

selfcheck.prompt: Why does 2×0 print two zero row sums while 0×3 prints an empty second line? Which loop tests determine that?
selfcheck.feedback: Two shapes may share a grand total yet have different row sums.

practice.title: Sums by row in a rectangle
practice.task: Read rows and cols in 0…10 and exactly rows*cols integers in -1000…1000. Print the total and a line of row sums; with rows=0 the second line is empty.
criteria: Compare 2×3 and 3×2 using the same six numbers. Check 0×3 and an input missing the final value.
Establish the shape before applying an index formula.
Do not test matrix code only with a square shape. Do not obtain cols from a[0] when there are no rows.
Add two cases of your own, including a rejection if the interface allows one. Explain one boundary result.
Keep the source, exact input and observed output.
practice.hint: Two shapes may share a grand total yet have different row sums.

steps.action: For 2×3 mark the boundaries between input rows. For 2×0 draw two empty rows.
steps.why: An equal number of elements does not imply an equal shape or report.
steps.expected: For 2×3, mark two groups of three values. For 2×0, mark two rows with no values.

steps.action: Validate both dimensions before scanning. Save the sum of a finished row even when the inner loop has zero iterations.
steps.why: The outer step selects the row; the inner step updates only that row's sum.
steps.expected: The starter prints 0 and 0 0 for the 2×3 case. With accumulation implemented the lines become 21 and 6 15.

steps.action: Compare 2×3 and 3×2 using the same six numbers. Check 0×3 and an input missing the final value.
steps.why: Swapping dimensions and testing empty dimensions exposes defects a square matrix hides.
steps.expected: For 0×3 the second line is blank; for 2×0 it is 0 0. A short input gives invalid.
